groups.sentence: Instructors should be able to show students knew the course rules; departures from stated restrictions can be evidence of violations.
Instructors do not rely on AI detection results as the sole evidence or basis for finding academic misconduct.
Instructors may gather evidence such as drafts, revision histories, process evidence, conversations with the student and course materials.
Detector output alone is insufficient to find a student responsible and does not determine responsibility.
Instructors may use detector results as supporting or preliminary evidence alongside other evidence in a broader case.
Instructors use multiple forms of evidence and a holistic approach when evaluating possible AI misuse.
Instructors base academic consequences and cases on clear, documented evidence of a violation.
Instructors review and verify suspected cases carefully and objectively, with human analysis, before reporting or taking action.
Misconduct findings require a standard of proof, such as clear and convincing evidence or more likely than not.
Instructors do not treat suspicion of student AI use as sufficient to find misconduct or assign a grade.
Instructors judge suspected misuse using course expectations, assignment requirements, student work and context.
No single indicator, score or artifact establishes AI use or authorship.
Instructors may use plagiarism or AI detection tools.
AI detection tools are not fully accurate or reliable indicators of AI use.
The burden of proof in academic misconduct cases lies with the university.
